means:
**1.** Existing **in name only** — the title is real, the power isn't. *The nominal head of the family.*
**2.** Of a price or sum: **token**, so small it's barely a real charge. *A nominal fee of £1.*
**3.** Technical (engineering, finance): **as specified, on-spec** — the stated or expected value, not the adjusted one. *Nominal wages, nominal thrust.*

Sense 1 is a quiet demotion. It doesn't accuse anyone of fraud — the label is genuine — it just drains it of substance, and it's usually said flatly by someone in a position to know. Sense 2 follows straight from it: a nominal fee is a price *in name only*, charged so the transaction exists on paper, not to make money.
trap: ⚠️ **nominal ≠ minimal.** *Minimal* just means very small. *Nominal* means small **because it's only a token** — the amount exists to name the thing, not to matter. A nominal charge is symbolic; a minimal charge is merely cheap.
trick_line: **NOM = name.** A nominal king is a king *in name*; a nominal fee is a price *in name*.
trick_unpack: Whatever follows the word is real on the label and hollow in fact.
sentences: The monarch remains the **nominal** commander of the armed forces, though no sovereign has issued an order in two centuries.
They charge a **nominal** two quid for the tour — basically just to stop people wandering in.
in_the_wild: NASA flight controllers: **"All systems are nominal."** Not \"good\" — *exactly as specified*. It's the word Mission Control keeps saying in *Apollo 13*, right up until things stop being nominal.
etymology: Latin **nomen, nominis** = *"name."* One root, a lot of GRE words: **nominate** (put a name forward), **nomenclature** (naming system), **misnomer** (wrong name), **denomination** (a named unit — of money or of church), and **ignominy** (*in-* "without" + *nomen* — namelessness, hence disgrace).
one_line: In name only; token-small; or exactly as specified.
